CLAIMSET Which forecast does each error measure reward? A simulation study of the functionals targeted by RMSE, MAE, MAPE and sMAPE
summary Which point forecast does each error measure reward? For 28 outcome distributions, candidate forecasts were fixed in advance from the true distribution (its quantiles, its mean and the minimisers of each measure's expected score) and scored by RMSE, MAE, MAPE and sMAPE. RMSE rewards the mean and MAE the median on every distribution. MAPE rewards a forecast below the median, far below on skewed outcomes. sMAPE rewards the median on lognormal and log-Laplace outcomes and a forecast close to it on the others, not a forecast above the mean; on counts it rewards zero when most outcomes are zero, and otherwise the median of the non-zero outcomes. In test sets of 6 to 18 outcomes, the forecast a measure ranks first varies so widely that it often lies near another measure's target; the choices settle from about 100 outcomes. The results test the recommendations of entrylib:2026.000008.

declarations funding: none | competing interests: Ivan Svetunkov runs EntryLib and wrote the review (entrylib:2026.000008) whose recommendations this study tests.
exploration 1 question; hypotheses 0; tests 0; runs 2: 1 confirmatory, 1 exploratory; lab record A2

DEFINITIONS
D1 [variable] RMSE: Root mean squared error of a point forecast f over a test set of outcomes y_1..y_n: sqrt(mean((y_t - f)^2)).
D2 [variable] MAE: Mean absolute error of a point forecast f over a test set: mean(|y_t - f|).
D3 [variable] MAPE: Mean absolute percentage error of a point forecast f over a test set: 100 mean(|y_t - f| / |y_t|), for outcomes of either sign. An outcome equal to zero makes it infinite for every forecast; where a distribution has positive density at zero, the expected MAPE of every forecast is infinite. Both are reported as infinite (Inf), not hidden. On counts it is not computed (decision DC3).
D4 [variable] sMAPE: Symmetric mean absolute percentage error of a point forecast f over a test set: 200 mean(|y_t - f| / (|y_t| + |f|)), where a pair with y_t = f (including y_t = f = 0) contributes 0.
D5 [concept] candidate forecast: A point forecast whose value is fixed before any test set is drawn and is the same for every test set. In this study each candidate is computed from the true outcome distribution (its mean, its median, the value with the lowest expected MAPE, the value with the lowest expected sMAPE, or zero); it is never estimated from a test set or from any other sample.
D6 [concept] expected score: The value a measure gives a candidate forecast in the limit of an infinitely long test set from the outcome distribution: for RMSE sqrt(E[(Y - f)^2]); for MAE E|Y - f|; for MAPE 100 E[|Y - f| / |Y| given Y != 0]; for sMAPE 200 E[|Y - f| / (|Y| + |f|)]. Computed from the distribution itself (by numerical integration, or exact sums for counts), not from simulated test sets.
D7 [concept] preferred candidate: Of the candidate forecasts for one outcome distribution, the one with the lowest expected score under a given measure. It says which candidate the measure rewards, independently of any test set.
D8 [concept] selection share: For one outcome distribution, one measure and one test-set size n: for each candidate forecast, the share of simulated test sets of n outcomes in which the measure gives that candidate the lowest score among all candidates (a tie between k candidates gives each 1/k). Its distribution over the candidates, and that distribution's mean, show where a test set of n outcomes puts the measure's choice. It is a count over test sets of a choice among fixed forecasts; it is not a test, and it is not about the value of the measure itself nor about any forecast estimated from data.
D9 [data] symmetric positive outcomes: Outcomes from a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 1, 5, 10 or 15, and from a Laplace distribution with location 100 and standard deviation 1, 2.5, 5 or 7.5 (scale sd / sqrt(2)): coefficients of variation from 1% to 15%. Mean and median are both 100. The Laplace stops at 7.5 because its exponential tail puts a share 0.5 exp(-sqrt(2) / CV) of outcomes at or below zero (about 3 in a billion at CV 0.075); outcomes at or below zero are counted as a diagnostic.
D10 [data] skewed positive outcomes: Outcomes y = 100 exp(x): lognormal (x normal with mean 0 and standard deviation s, s = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1) and log-Laplace (x Laplace with location 0 and scale b, b = 0.25, 0.5); and gamma outcomes with mean 100 and shape 2, 5 or 20. All are positive with a density that vanishes at zero, so the expected MAPE is finite.
D11 [data] outcomes with outliers: Symmetric outliers: 95% of outcomes from N(100, 5^2) and 5% from N(100, 15^2). Upward spikes: outcomes from N(100, 5^2), of which 5% are multiplied by 3, as from promotions.
D12 [data] count outcomes: Poisson counts with mean 1.5, 3.5 or 10.
D13 [data] intermittent outcomes: Counts of which more than half are zero: negative binomial with size 1 and mean 0.3, 0.5 or 0.6, and Poisson with mean 0.3, 0.5 or 0.65. MAPE is not computed on counts.
D14 [design] selection design: For each outcome distribution, the candidate forecasts are fixed first, and their expected scores computed (continuous distributions: from one reference sample of 10,000,000 outcomes drawn once with its own seed; counts: exactly, from the probability mass function). Then, for each test-set size n = 10, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1,000 and 100,000, test sets of n outcomes are drawn (1,000 for each size under 100,000, 200 at 100,000); in each, every candidate is scored by every measure, and the candidate with the lowest score is counted as that measure's choice (a tie between k candidates counts 1/k for each). No forecast is estimated from a test set.

EVIDENCE
E1 [simulation; runs 1000] A simulation of which fixed candidate forecast each error measure ranks first. For each of 28 outcome distributions (normal and Laplace at level 100 with standard deviations 1 to 15; lognormal, log-Laplace and gamma; normal with symmetric outliers or upward spikes; Poisson counts; intermittent counts with more than half zeros), the candidates are fixed before any test set is drawn: the quantiles at levels 0.01 to 0.99, the mean, and the values that minimise the expected MAPE (continuous outcomes only) and the expected sMAPE, merged where equal. Their expected scores come from one reference sample of 10,000,000 outcomes (continuous) or exact sums (counts); the candidate with the lowest expected score is each measure's preferred candidate. Then 1,000 test sets of each size n (6, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 24, 36, 48, 100, 250, 500, 1,000, 10,000) are drawn, every candidate is scored by RMSE, MAE, MAPE and sMAPE, and the candidate with the lowest score is counted as that measure's choice (a tie of k candidates counts 1/k each). No forecast is estimated from data. T1 gives each distribution's mean, median and share of zeros; T2 each measure's preferred candidate; T3 the percentiles of the chosen candidates' quantile levels (or values, for counts) over test sets; the results give their means and the share of test sets choosing the preferred candidate. Run RN1 under plan PL1.R4 (event PL4).

LIMITATIONS
L1 [sampling; affects C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C10, C11; reduces_transferability; mitigation none] The test sets are independent draws from a fixed distribution. Real forecast errors are often correlated (forecasts of several horizons from one origin) and their distribution can change over a test period, so a real test set carries less information than the same number of outcomes here, and the choices spread more.
L2 [model_specification; affects C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C10, C11; reduces_transferability; mitigation none] The candidates are fixed functionals of known distributions; no forecast is estimated from data. The results say which forecast each measure rewards and how reliably a test set shows it, not how forecasts estimated from data behave.
L3 [measurement; affects C2; reduces_precision; mitigation none] Log-Laplace outcomes with b = 0.5 have infinite variance, so the expected RMSE of every candidate is infinite. The mean is still the preferred candidate of RMSE there, since the difference in expected squared error between two candidates is finite and favours the one nearer the mean; the expected RMSE values the run computed for this distribution are artefacts of the finite reference sample.
L4 [measurement; affects C4; reduces_precision; mitigation none] Normal and Laplace outcomes have a small positive density at zero, so their expected MAPE is, strictly, infinite. At the levels used (7 to 100 standard deviations above zero) no outcome at or below zero was drawn (T1), and the effect on the computed values is negligible.
L5 [measurement; affects C8, C9, C10, C11; reduces_precision; mitigation none] The candidates are the quantiles at levels 0.01 apart, the mean and the minimisers, so a choice is resolved to the nearest candidate; spreads of choices narrower than about 0.01 quantile levels are not resolved.
L6 [researcher_position; affects C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C10, C11; could_bias_magnitude; mitigation none] The study was designed and run by an agent under the supervision of the guarantor, who also wrote the review whose claims it tests (entrylib:2026.000008); no search was made for other simulation studies of these measures.

OPEN QUESTIONS
O1 [from C5, C6] Why does sMAPE prefer the median when the logarithm of the outcome is symmetric, a forecast slightly away from it otherwise, and the median of the non-zero outcomes on counts with fewer than half zeros? An analytical treatment, with further simulations, is left to a separate study.

ARTEFACTS
A1 [data] Every result of the lab record (10546 results of 2 runs) at full precision: the lab result's ID, its run, the quantity as the run's script named it, its conditions and its value (both as JSON). The evidence's tables give the values to four significant digits.
A2 [lab_record] Lab record of the study: questions, hypotheses, plans, runs, results and decisions, as an append-only, hash-chained event log (Claimset lab record specification v0.22, begun 2026-11-15; exported with claimset 0.44.0).
A3 [code] The simulation code at the commit run RN1 ran: settings.py (the 28 outcome distributions), reference.py (the candidate forecasts and their expected scores), measures.py (the four measures on fixed candidates), simulate.py (the selection design), plot.py (the figures) and test_rankings.py (checks against exact results).
